statement: The function returns a result r such that r is exactly the list of all integers n with low <= n <= high and sequential_digits(n), in strictly increasing order. Here sequential_digits(n) means there exist an integer k >= 2 and digits d_0, ..., d_{k-1} such that 1 <= d_0 <= 9, 0 <= d_i <= 9 for every i, d_{i+1} = d_i + 1 for every 0 <= i < k-1, and n = sum_{i=0}^{k-1} d_i * 10^{k-1-i}. Equivalently: (a) for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), low <= r[i] <= high and sequential_digits(r[i]); (b) for every n with low <= n <= high and sequential_digits(n), there is exactly one i with 0 <= i < len(r) and r[i] = n; (c) for every i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), r[i] < r[j].
preconditions: low and high are 64-bit integers with 10 <= low <= high <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), low <= r[i] <= high.
preconditions: low and high are 64-bit integers with 10 <= low <= high <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), r[i] has sequential digits; that is, r[i] >= 10 and in the usual decimal notation of r[i] without leading zeros, every digit after the first is exactly one greater than the digit immediately before it.
preconditions: low and high are 64-bit integers with 10 <= low <= high <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer n with low <= n <= high that has sequential digits, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that r[i] = n.
preconditions: low and high are 64-bit integers with 10 <= low <= high <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is strictly increasing: for every i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), r[i] < r[j].
preconditions: low and high are 64-bit integers with 10 <= low <= high <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) is the number of integers n such that low <= n <= high and n has sequential digits.
preconditions: low and high are 64-bit integers with 10 <= low <= high <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = 0 if and only if there is no integer n with low <= n <= high that has sequential digits.
preconditions: low and high are 64-bit integers with 10 <= low <= high <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and len(r) > 0, r[0] is the least integer n satisfying low <= n <= high and n has sequential digits; that is, r[0] satisfies low <= r[0] <= high, has sequential digits, and for every integer n with low <= n <= high and sequential digits, r[0] <= n.
preconditions: low and high are 64-bit integers with 10 <= low <= high <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and len(r) > 0, r[len(r)-1] is the greatest integer n satisfying low <= n <= high and n has sequential digits; that is, r[len(r)-1] satisfies low <= r[len(r)-1] <= high, has sequential digits, and for every integer n with low <= n <= high and sequential digits, n <= r[len(r)-1].
preconditions: low and high are 64-bit integers with 10 <= low <= high <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r)-1, there is no integer n such that low <= n <= high, n has sequential digits, and r[i] < n < r[i+1].
preconditions: low and high are 64-bit integers with 10 <= low <= high <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) <= 36.
preconditions: low and high are 64-bit integers with 10 <= low <= high <= 10^9.
